flashcards.front: Maximum Power Transfer Theorem (AC Circuit with complex source impedance Z_s = R_s + jX_s)
flashcards.back:
For maximum average power transfer to load Z_L = R_L + jX_L:
1) If both R_L and X_L are variable: Z_L = Z_s* = R_s - jX_s, and P_max = |V_th|^2 / (4 * R_s).
2) If only R_L is variable: R_L = sqrt(R_s^2 + (X_s + X_L)^2).

flashcards.front: Conditions for Reciprocity and Symmetry in Two-Port Networks (Z, Y, ABCD, h)
flashcards.back:
• Z-parameters: Symmetric if Z11 = Z22; Reciprocal if Z12 = Z21
• Y-parameters: Symmetric if Y11 = Y22; Reciprocal if Y12 = Y21
• ABCD (T): Symmetric if A = D; Reciprocal if AD - BC = 1
• h-parameters: Symmetric if Δh = h11*h22 - h12*h21 = 1; Reciprocal if h12 = -h21

flashcards.front: Quality Factor (Q) and Bandwidth (BW) in Series vs Parallel RLC Resonance
flashcards.back:
• Resonant frequency: ω_0 = 1 / sqrt(LC)
• Series RLC: Q = (ω_0 * L) / R = (1 / R) * sqrt(L / C)
• Parallel RLC: Q = R / (ω_0 * L) = R * sqrt(C / L)
• Bandwidth: BW = ω_0 / Q (rad/s) or f_0 / Q (Hz)

flashcards.front: BIBO Stability Condition for Continuous-Time and Discrete-Time LTI Systems
flashcards.back:
• Continuous-Time: Impulse response h(t) must be absolutely integrable: ∫_{-∞}^{∞} |h(t)| dt < ∞ (ROC of H(s) includes the jω axis).
• Discrete-Time: Impulse response h[n] must be absolutely summable: ∑_{n=-∞}^{∞} |h[n]| < ∞ (ROC of H(z) includes the unit circle |z| = 1).

flashcards.front: Nyquist Sampling Rate for Bandpass Signals vs Lowpass Signals
flashcards.back:
• Lowpass signal with max frequency f_m: f_s >= 2 * f_m
• Bandpass signal (f_L to f_H, bandwidth B = f_H - f_L): Minimum sampling rate without aliasing is f_s = (2 * f_H) / k, where k = floor(f_H / B).

flashcards.front: Initial Value Theorem (IVT) & Final Value Theorem (FVT) in Laplace and Z-Domain
flashcards.back:
• Laplace: x(0+) = lim_{s→∞} sX(s); x(∞) = lim_{s→0} sX(s) (valid only if all poles of sX(s) are strictly in LHP).
• Causal Z-Transform: x[0] = lim_{z→∞} X(z); x[∞] = lim_{z→1} (z - 1)X(z) (valid if poles of (z-1)X(z) are strictly inside unit circle).

flashcards.front: Peak Overshoot (%Mp) and Settling Time (ts) for Standard 2nd Order Underdamped System
flashcards.back:
• %Mp = 100 * exp(-π * ζ / sqrt(1 - ζ^2))
• Peak Time: t_p = π / ω_d, where ω_d = ω_n * sqrt(1 - ζ^2)
• Settling Time: t_s (2% tolerance) = 4 / (ζ * ω_n); t_s (5% tolerance) = 3 / (ζ * ω_n)

flashcards.front: Nyquist Stability Criterion Formula: Z = N + P
flashcards.back:
• Z = Number of closed-loop poles in Right Half s-Plane (must be 0 for stability)
• P = Number of open-loop poles of G(s)H(s) in RHP
• N = Number of clockwise encirclements of (-1 + j0) by the Nyquist plot of G(s)H(s) (if contour is clockwise). Counter-clockwise encirclements are negative.

flashcards.front: Kalman Controllability & Observability Test for State-Space Model (A, B, C, D)
flashcards.back:
• Controllability Matrix: Q_c = [B  AB  A^2B ... A^(n-1)B]. System is completely state controllable iff rank(Q_c) = n.
• Observability Matrix: Q_o = [C^T  A^TC^T ... (A^T)^(n-1)C^T]. System is completely observable iff rank(Q_o) = n.
• State Transition Matrix: Φ(t) = e^(At) = L^-1[(sI - A)^-1].

flashcards.front: Maximum Clock Frequency (Minimum Clock Period T_clk) in Synchronous Sequential Circuits
flashcards.back:
T_clk >= t_pcq (FF propagation delay) + t_comb (max combinational logic delay) + t_setup (FF setup time) - t_skew (if clock skew aids).
Hold time constraint: t_ccq + t_comb_min >= t_hold + t_skew.

flashcards.front: Comparison of Flash ADC, SAR ADC, and Dual-Slope ADC
flashcards.back:
• Flash ADC: Fastest (1 clock cycle), requires 2^n - 1 comparators & 2^n resistors.
• SAR (Successive Approximation) ADC: Conversion time = n * T_clk (independent of input amplitude).
• Dual-Slope Integrating ADC: Highest noise immunity & accuracy, slowest (up to 2^(n+1) * T_clk).

flashcards.front: Properties of Eigenvalues (λ_i) of an n × n Matrix A
flashcards.back:
1) Sum of eigenvalues: ∑ λ_i = Trace(A)
2) Product of eigenvalues: ∏ λ_i = det(A)
3) Eigenvalues of A^T are same as A
4) Eigenvalues of A^-1 are 1/λ_i; Eigenvalues of A^k are (λ_i)^k
5) Symmetric/Hermitian matrices always have real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenvectors.

flashcards.front: Cauchy's Residue Theorem & Residue at a Pole of Order m
flashcards.back:
• ∮_C f(z) dz = 2πi * ∑ [Residues of f(z) at poles inside C]
• Simple pole at z = a: Res(f, a) = lim_{z→a} (z - a)f(z)
• Pole of order m at z = a: Res(f, a) = [1 / (m-1)!] * lim_{z→a} d^(m-1)/dz^(m-1) [(z - a)^m f(z)].

flashcards.front: Number of Derangements D(n) (No item goes into its original position)
Effect of Negative Feedback Topologies on Input Impedance (R_if) and Output Impedance (R_of)
flashcards.back:
• Series-Shunt (Voltage Amplifier): R_if increases by (1+Aβ), R_of decreases by (1+Aβ)
• Shunt-Series (Current Amplifier): R_if decreases, R_of increases
• Series-Series (Transconductance): R_if increases, R_of increases
• Shunt-Shunt (Transresistance): R_if decreases, R_of decreases
(Trick: Series at port -> Impedance increases; Shunt at port -> Impedance decreases)

flashcards.front: Op-Amp Slew Rate Limiting & Maximum Undistorted Sine Wave Frequency
flashcards.back:
For output V_o(t) = V_m * sin(2πft), max slope is 2πf * V_m.
To avoid slew-rate distortion:
2π * f_max * V_m <= SR (in V/s)
f_max = SR / (2π * V_m).

flashcards.front: Transmission Line Input Impedance, Reflection Coefficient (Γ) & VSWR
flashcards.back:
• Γ_L = (Z_L - Z_0) / (Z_L + Z_0)
• VSWR (s) = (1 + |Γ_L|) / (1 - |Γ_L|)
• Z_in(l) = Z_0 * [Z_L + j*Z_0*tan(βl)] / [Z_0 + j*Z_L*tan(βl)]
• Quarter-Wave Transformer (l = λ/4): Z_in = (Z_0)^2 / Z_L.

flashcards.front: Rectangular Waveguide Cutoff Frequency (f_c), Dominant Mode & Velocity Relations
flashcards.back:
• f_c(m,n) = (v / 2) * sqrt((m/a)^2 + (n/b)^2)
• For a > b, Dominant mode is TE_10 with f_c = v / (2a) and λ_c = 2a.
• Phase velocity v_p = v / sqrt(1 - (f_c/f)^2); Group velocity v_g = v * sqrt(1 - (f_c/f)^2); v_p * v_g = v^2.

flashcards.front: Einstein Relation, Built-in Potential (V_bi) and Depletion Width (W) in PN Junction
flashcards.back:
• Einstein Relation: D_n / μ_n = D_p / μ_p = kT / q = V_T (~25.9 mV at 300 K)
• Built-in Potential: V_bi = V_T * ln((N_A * N_D) / n_i^2)
• Depletion Width: W = sqrt([2ε_s / q] * [1/N_A + 1/N_D] * (V_bi - V_A)); penetration satisfies N_A * x_p = N_D * x_n.

flashcards.front: MOS Capacitor Regimes (p-type substrate) and Threshold Voltage condition
flashcards.back:
For p-substrate (V_FB = Φ_ms - Q_ox/C_ox):
• V_G < V_FB: Accumulation (holes at surface)
• V_FB < V_G < V_T: Depletion (negative acceptor ions exposed)
• V_G >= V_T: Strong Inversion when surface potential ψ_s = 2*φ_F = 2*V_T*ln(N_A / n_i).

flashcards.front: Carson's Rule for FM Bandwidth, PCM SQNR (dB), and Shannon-Hartley Capacity
flashcards.back:
• FM Bandwidth (Carson): BW = 2 * (Δf + f_m) = 2 * f_m * (β + 1), where β = Δf / f_m
• Sinusoidal n-bit Uniform PCM: SQNR_dB = 1.76 + 6.02 * n (dB)
• AWGN Channel Capacity: C = B * log_2(1 + S / (N_0 * B)) bits/sec (as B → ∞, C_max = 1.44 * (S / N_0)).

flashcards.front: Matched Filter Impulse Response, Maximum Output SNR, and BPSK Bit Error Probability
flashcards.back:
• For signal s(t) of duration T in AWGN (PSD = N_0 / 2): Matched filter impulse response h(t) = s(T - t).
• Max Output SNR at t = T depends ONLY on signal energy: SNR_max = 2E / N_0.
• Probability of bit error for Coherent BPSK & QPSK: P_e = Q(sqrt(2 * E_b / N_0)).

flashcards.front: Instruction Pipeline Speedup, CPI with Stalls, and Cache Average Memory Access Time (AMAT)
flashcards.back:
• Ideal k-stage pipeline speedup = k. With stall cycles per instruction: CPI = 1 + (stall frequency * stall cycles).
• Simultaneous access AMAT = h * t_cache + (1 - h) * t_main
• Hierarchical access AMAT = t_cache + (1 - h) * t_main (where h = hit ratio).

quizQuestions.question: A source with impedance Z_s = (4 + j3) Ω is connected to a purely resistive variable load R_L. For maximum power transfer to R_L, the value of R_L should be:
quizQuestions.explanation: When the load is restricted to be purely resistive (X_L = 0), maximum power transfer occurs at R_L = |Z_s| = sqrt(R_s^2 + X_s^2) = sqrt(4^2 + 3^2) = 5 Ω.

quizQuestions.question: In a series RLC circuit at resonance, the source voltage is 10 V (rms) and the quality factor Q is 25. The voltage across the capacitor at resonance is:
quizQuestions.explanation: At series resonance, V_L = V_C = Q * V_source = 25 * 10 V = 250 V (voltage magnification).

quizQuestions.question: A continuous-time signal x(t) = cos(200πt) + sin(500πt) is sampled at 400 Hz and passed through an ideal low-pass reconstruction filter with cutoff frequency 250 Hz. The output frequencies present are:
quizQuestions.explanation: Input frequencies are f1 = 100 Hz and f2 = 250 Hz. With f_s = 400 Hz, f1 = 100 Hz (< 200 Hz) has no aliasing. f2 = 250 Hz (> f_s/2 = 200 Hz) aliases to |f_s - f2| = |400 - 250| = 150 Hz. Both 100 Hz and 150 Hz pass through the 250 Hz LPF.

quizQuestions.question: A causal LTI discrete-time system has transfer function H(z) = (z + 0.5) / ((z - 0.8)(z + 1.2)). Is the system BIBO stable?
options: Yes, because both zeros are inside unit circle
No, because a pole at z = -1.2 lies outside the unit circle
quizQuestions.explanation: A causal LTI system is BIBO stable if and only if all poles lie strictly inside the unit circle |z| < 1. Here, the pole at z = -1.2 has magnitude 1.2 > 1, so it is unstable.

quizQuestions.question: A unity negative feedback system has open-loop transfer function G(s) = K / [s(s + 2)(s + 4)]. The value of K at which the system is marginally stable is:
quizQuestions.explanation: Characteristic equation: s^3 + 6s^2 + 8s + K = 0. For a 3rd-order Routh array, marginal stability occurs when the product of inner terms equals product of outer terms: K = 6 * 8 = 48.

quizQuestions.question: Adding a zero in the open left-half s-plane to an open-loop transfer function generally:
options: Bends the root locus towards the right-half plane and reduces stability
Bends the root locus towards the left-half plane and improves relative stability
Increases the system type number by 1
Decreases the bandwidth of the system
quizQuestions.explanation: Adding a left-half plane zero (like a PD controller or Lead compensator) pulls the root locus toward the left, increasing damping and improving relative stability.

quizQuestions.question: What is the minimum number of 2-to-1 Multiplexers required to implement a 16-to-1 Multiplexer (without using any extra gates)?
quizQuestions.explanation: To build an N:1 MUX using 2:1 MUXes, the total required is N - 1 = 16 - 1 = 15 (8 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 15).

quizQuestions.question: A 4-bit Johnson (twisted-ring) counter is initialized to 0000 and clocked at 120 MHz. What is the frequency of the output at any flip-flop?
quizQuestions.explanation: An n-bit Johnson counter is a MOD-2n counter. For n = 4, it has 2*4 = 8 distinct states, so f_out = f_clk / (2n) = 120 MHz / 8 = 15 MHz.

quizQuestions.question: If the eigenvalues of a 3×3 matrix A are 1, 2, and 4, then the determinant of (A^-1)^T is:
quizQuestions.explanation: det(A) = product of eigenvalues = 1 * 2 * 4 = 8. Since det(A^T) = det(A) and det(A^-1) = 1/det(A), det((A^-1)^T) = 1/8.

quizQuestions.question: Four letters are randomly placed into four addressed envelopes (one in each). What is the probability that NO letter goes into its correct envelope?
quizQuestions.explanation: Total ways = 4! = 24. Number of derangements of 4 items D(4) = 9. Probability = 9 / 24 = 3 / 8.

quizQuestions.question: An Op-Amp has a slew rate of 2π V/μs. What is the maximum peak amplitude V_m of a 500 kHz sinusoidal output signal without slew-rate distortion?
A lossless 50 Ω transmission line is terminated in a load impedance of 100 Ω. The Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) on the line is:
quizQuestions.explanation: For a purely resistive load R_L on a lossless line Z_0, VSWR = max(R_L/Z_0, Z_0/R_L) = 100 / 50 = 2.0.

quizQuestions.question: In a silicon sample at 300 K (n_i = 1.5 × 10^10 cm^-3), donor concentration is N_D = 1.5 × 10^16 cm^-3. The thermal equilibrium hole concentration p_0 is:
A speech signal bandlimited to 4 kHz is sampled at 1.25 times the Nyquist rate and quantized using an 8-bit uniform PCM system. The resulting bit rate is:
quizQuestions.explanation: Nyquist rate = 2 * f_m = 8 kHz. Sampling rate f_s = 1.25 * 8 kHz = 10 kHz. Bit rate R_b = n * f_s = 8 bits/sample * 10,000 samples/sec = 80 kbps.

quizQuestions.question: A system has an L1 cache with 2 ns access time and a 95% hit ratio, and main memory with 60 ns access time (hierarchical access). What is the Average Memory Access Time (AMAT)?
quizQuestions.explanation: In hierarchical access, AMAT = t_cache + (1 - h) * t_main = 2 ns + (0.05 * 60 ns) = 2 + 3 = 5.0 ns.
